items.headline: Dollar firms into the NY close — DXY ~101.86 (+0.1%), EUR/USD ~1.1184, GBP/USD ~1.3417, USD/JPY ~158.46 (+0.34%) as the JOLTS beat (7.523M) + factory orders beat (+1.8%) lift Dec Fed hike pricing to ~79%
JOLTS BEATS: September openings 7.523M (vs 7.11M fcst, Aug revised to 7.19M); openings rate 4.5%, hires 5.402M, layoffs 1.641M (lowest since Mar 2025) — 10Y touched 4.97% after the release
Factory orders BEAT: September +1.8% m/m (vs +1.2% fcst, prev +0.3%); durable goods +1.9%, nondefense cap goods ex-aircraft +0.6% — second firm US print at 9:00am CT

Macklem restates the BoC line: 'further rate hikes may be needed' but proceed carefully, meeting by meeting; CPI seen ~3.5% by year-end, at/above 3% through much of 2027; Dec hike ~56% — USD/CAD ~1.3993, little changed as oil swings overshadowed the tone

Oil round-trips: Brent's London bounce to $106.61 / WTI $98.06 faded intraday to ~$104.7 / ~$96.6 on unconfirmed US-Iran deal speculation; Iran denied being close to a deal, no agreement announced — gold ~$3,955, second straight gain off Friday's $3,870 low
Dollar drifts in London into the US midterms — EUR/USD $1.1201 (+0.14%), GBP/USD $1.3421 (+0.1%), USD/JPY 157.80, USD/CHF 0.8164 (-0.3%) as the franc firms on the CPI beat
Oil rebounds in London — Brent $106.61 (+1.76%), WTI $98.06 (+1.66%) at 0744 GMT as an Iranian official says a deal is far off after the US strike on Qeshm Island
Swiss franc firms after CPI beat — USD/CHF 0.8164, EUR/CHF 0.9137 (lowest since June); CPI 1.5% y/y, highest since Dec 2023, energy-led, core 0.5% unchanged
Aussie extends post-RBA slide — AUD/USD $0.6963 (-0.5%) in London after the 6-3 hike to 4.85%; yuan slips as the PBoC move bites, USD/CNH ~6.67
No 7:30am CT US release today — JOLTS (fcst 7.11M) and factory orders land 9:00am CT, the last labor read before Friday payrolls
Gold eases to ~$3,927 in London as Dec Fed hike bets (~75%) hold; US 10Y ~4.91%
RBA hikes 25bp to 4.85% in a 6-3 split - fifth hike of 2026, highest since Dec 2008; Bullock gives no guidance, 'probably good to take stock'
Aussie slips below $0.70 after the split hike - AUD/USD $0.6974 low, ~$0.6978 in Asia, a two-week low
PBoC moves to slow the yuan's rise - FX deposit reserve ratio to 6% from 4% from Nov 15; offshore yuan slips ~0.3%, USD/CNH ~6.67
Oil bounces ~0.5% in Asia after US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island reported - Brent ~$105.25, WTI ~$96.93, after Monday's >7% slide
Dollar steadies in Asia - DXY ~101.81, EUR/USD ~$1.1182, GBP/USD ~$1.3401, USD/JPY ~157.92 ahead of the US midterms
Today: Swiss CPI 1:30am CT, US midterms, JOLTS 9:00am CT, Macklem 10:00am CT, NZ Q3 jobs 3:45pm CT

ISM manufacturing BEATS at 55.5 (vs 54.5 fcst, prev 54.5) — production 59.0, prices paid eased to 75.2 — but the dollar did not react (DXY ~101.60 at release, FXStreet); sentiment worsened a third month (66% negative)

Oil slide extends into the NY close — Brent ~$108.41 (-4.4%), WTI ~$99.60 (-4.3%) as a draft proposal to end the US-Iran war circulated after Iranian negotiators left Doha; Goldman still sees Brent $140 in 2027 if Gulf output stays 3.5M b/d below 2025 average

Dollar softer into the close — DXY ~101.68 (-0.27%, low 101.44), EUR/USD ~1.1194 (high 1.1237), GBP/USD ~1.3412 (high 1.3448) as falling oil and lower yields (10Y ~4.92%) outweighed the ISM beat ahead of Tuesday's US midterms
